key_insight: Fine-tuning an already-aligned language model on benign tasks can unexpectedly break its safety guards because the assumed orthogonality between task updates and safety-critical directions is not robust — gradient-descent dynamics cause that orthogonality to collapse.
problem_solved: Explains why safety guardrails degrade unpredictably after benign fine-tuning and debunks the common reassurance that fine-tuning updates remain harmlessly orthogonal to safety directions; identifies a geometric and dynamical mechanism behind alignment collapse.
method: Geometric analysis of parameter-space directions to characterize ‘safety-critical’ subspaces and the structural instability of orthogonality assumptions.
Dynamical study of gradient-descent trajectories showing how small perturbations and optimization dynamics cause collapse of orthogonality.
Empirical validation on language models: fine-tuning on benign tasks leads to measurable drops in safety metrics despite no harmful training data; propose diagnostics and mitigation directions.
impact: Practitioners can’t rely on orthogonality as a safety guarantee — fine-tuning may silently erode alignment even when data is benign. This calls for active safety monitoring, robustness-aware fine-tuning methods (e.g., constrained optimization, regularization or safety checkpoints), and new diagnostics for alignment stability.
visual_elements: Parameter-space diagram showing an aligned model, a safety-critical subspace, and the idealized orthogonal update vs the collapsed (non-orthogonal) update.
Trajectory plot of gradient-descent steps illustrating how optimization dynamics move updates into safety directions (alignment collapse over time).
Before/after bar chart of safety metrics (e.g., harmful-response rate) showing degradation after benign fine-tuning.
Flowchart of practical mitigations: detect → diagnose (alignment stability test) → apply constrained fine-tuning or rollback.
paper_title: The Geometry of Alignment Collapse: When Fine-Tuning Breaks Safety
paper_authors: Max Springer, Chung Peng Lee, Blossom Metevier, Jane Castleman, Bohdan Turbal
